![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14217845/assets/a1e4a1e39c85a037f3f4f49910b651300363ef34bee969464f5e711aa00986e3.png)

Evaluate the triple integral 
${∭}_{R}4{x}^{2}z\,dV$
over the region $R,$ shown above.

*Hint: All surfaces, except for the right one, are parallel to the corresponding coordinate planes.*
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14217845/assets/9165163be9ce95e7165f04d26e6ce8080699ab4d477eba3f804c849fdf1fb679.png)

 

Notice that our solid can be written as the type III region

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,\,0\le y\le 4-z\},
$$

where

$$
D=\{(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le 3\}
$$

is the projection of $R$ onto the $xz$-plane, shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14217845/assets/ca74bf149c1371fe9f1622586d9eb92fe180a9c9bb6a0c53d16f538b3c55f4a4.png)

Hence, the type III representation of $R$ is

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le 3,\,\,0\le y\le 4-z\}
$$

As a result, by writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}4{x}^{2}z\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{4-z}4{x}^{2}z\,dy\,dz\,dx.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y$, treating $x$ and $z$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{4-z}4{x}^{2}z\,dy\,dz\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{3}[{\int }_{0}^{4-z}4{x}^{2}z\,dy]dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{3}4{x}^{2}z[y]_{y=0}^{y=4-z}\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{3}4{x}^{2}z(4-z)\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{3}(16{x}^{2}z-4{x}^{2}{z}^{2})\,dz\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z$, treating $x$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{3}(16{x}^{2}z-4{x}^{2}{z}^{2})\,dz\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{3}(16{x}^{2}z-4{x}^{2}{z}^{2})\,dz]dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[8{x}^{2}{z}^{2}-\frac{4}{3}{x}^{2}{z}^{3}]_{z=0}^{z=3}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}36{x}^{2}\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}36{x}^{2}\,dx & ={[12{x}^{3}]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =(12-0) \\  & =12.\end{aligned}
$$
